title: Unit – 5 : Session – 3 : SLO – 2  |  Graph Traversal — Breadth First Search (BFS)
sections: I. Fill in the Blanks
BFS stands for BREADTH FIRST SEARCH.
BFS uses QUEUE data structure for its implementation.
In BFS, a vertex is marked as VISITED when it has been visited.
The time complexity of BFS for a graph with V vertices and E edges is O(V + E).
BFS is suitable for finding the SHORTEST path in an unweighted graph.
II. True or False
BFS visits the deepest unvisited node first — FALSE (it visits level by level).
BFS can be used to detect cycles in an undirected graph — TRUE.
BFS uses a queue data structure — TRUE.
In BFS, each vertex is visited exactly once — TRUE.
III. Short Answer Questions
BFS: a traversal that starts at a vertex, visits all its immediate neighbours first, then the neighbours'
neighbours, level by level, using a queue.
Applications: shortest path in unweighted graphs; social-network friend suggestions; also peer-to-peer
network search and web crawling.
Data structure: QUEUE.
DFS vs BFS: DFS goes deep first using a stack; BFS explores breadth/level-wise using a queue and
guarantees shortest hop-count paths in unweighted graphs.
IV. Solve and Write — Given Undirected Graph (A-H)
Adjacency list:
A -> B, C    B -> A, D, E    C -> A, F, G    D -> B, H
E -> B, H    F -> C, H       G -> C, H       H -> D, E, F, G
BFS traversal from A (neighbours in alphabetical order): A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H
Iterative BFS internally uses a QUEUE.
